item.content:encoded:
Brazil wonders: Where on earth is Flavio Bolsonaro? Reuters | Updated: 27-10-2026 21:16 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 21:16 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Brazil canceled Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's passports on Tuesday, after he failed to comply with a Supreme Court order to turn them in, according to two sources from the federal police, which is trying to locate the former presidential candidate. Meanwhile, Argentina said it had no record of him entering its territory and the right-wing senator's aides either declined to say where he was or said they did not know. Bolsonaro was favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. On Monday, he was given 24 hours to hand in his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing, but that deadline has now lapsed, the two sources said, leading to his documents being canceled. The mystery over his whereabouts has raised concerns he could follow the path of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who moved to the United States after refusing to concede losing to Lula in 2022. He eventually returned to Brazil but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup. His son has yet to officially concede defeat — saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities — but his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged Lula's victory. Argentina's government said it had no record of Bolsonaro entering the country. Following media reports about a private plane at Iguazu International Airport on the Argentina-Brazil border, Argentine authorities checked the aircraft and its crew, finding no flight plan listing the Bolsonaro family, the statement added. A spokesperson for right-wing Argentine President Javier Milei, who has yet to congratulate Lula on his victory, said, "There is no asylum request," declining to give further details. Meanwhile, a senior Brazilian Federal Police official said Bolsonaro has not exited the country via any regular migration point. Brazilians only need an ID card, rather than a passport, to enter neighboring Argentina. Right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo, who serves as a sort of unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined to answer questions about Bolsonaro's whereabouts. "After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to the press," he said in a message. "If I have any comments to make on any matter, I will get in touch." Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move. "If my brother does not win, I'm in favor that he would leave the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder on October 23. Another source close to Bolsonaro said they could not reach him. "I tried to talk to Flavio this morning by phone," they said. "It rang and it rang, but he didn't pick up."

item.content:encoded:
Keanu Reeves replaces Alan Ritchson in action thriller 'Maelstrom' Hollywood star Keanu Reeves is set to headline the upcoming Netflix action film 'Maelstrom', taking over the lead role from 'Reacher' star Alan Ritchson, who has exited the project for undisclosed reasons.  ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 19:29 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 19:29 IST

Keanu Reeves (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Hollywood star Keanu Reeves is set to headline the upcoming Netflix action film 'Maelstrom', taking over the lead role from 'Reacher' star Alan Ritchson, who has exited the project for undisclosed reasons. Deadline confirmed the news that Keanu Reeves is now set to lead the feature, which is directed by Jaume Collet-Serra, known for his work on Carry-On. In 'Maelstrom', Keanu Reeves will play a Federal Marshal assigned to protect the fiancée of an arms dealer turned witness. According to Deadline, the character must defend her through one brutal night as a hurricane cuts off communication, strands them without reinforcements, and unleashes the dealer’s men on their safe house. The current draft of the script is written by Mark Bianculli, following an initial draft by the late Gregory Fitzpatrick. The project has a lengthy history in Hollywood, having originally been set up as a spec script at Warner Bros. back in 1993. Jeff Robinov is set to produce alongside Tabitha Shick of Talking Pictures. Coming off the fourth instalment of the 'John Wick' franchise, Reeves has continued to expand his active slate of projects. His upcoming ventures include entering talks to lead James Wan’s take on the South Korean crime actioner 'The Gangster', 'The Cop', 'The Devil' for Paramount, reprising his voice role as Shadow in 'Sonic the Hedgehog 4', and starring in an adaptation of the forthcoming Oliver Lowe novel Kill Current: A Jon Hendricks Thriller under his new banner, Two Dragonflies. Additional upcoming projects for Reeves include the Warner Bros. sci-fi film 'Shiver' and 'The Entertainment System Is Down' from director Ruben Ostlund. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Tibet, Uyghur rights concerns raised in Geneva with China amid fears over minority freedoms According to the CTA, in a statement, the Tibet Bureau expressed appreciation to the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) for addressing concerns related to Tibet, Xinjiang, Hong Kong and the possible impact of China’s ethnic unity legislation on minority communities. ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 17:26 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 17:26 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) raised concerns over human rights violations and restrictions affecting Tibetans and Uyghurs during the 19th round of the Swiss-Chinese Bilateral Human Rights Dialogue held on October 19 and 20, 2026, as reported by the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA). According to the CTA, in a statement, the Tibet Bureau expressed appreciation to the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) for addressing concerns related to Tibet, Xinjiang, Hong Kong and the possible impact of China’s ethnic unity legislation on minority communities. Switzerland’s intervention was an important step towards keeping Tibet’s human rights situation on the international agenda. According to the FDFA’s announcement on October 20, the discussions covered the implications of China’s so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” for the linguistic, cultural and religious rights of minority groups. Individual human rights cases were also raised during the dialogue. The Swiss delegation was led by Dagmar Schmidt Tartagli, Deputy Head of the FDFA’s Peace and Human Rights Division, while Yuan Yuan, Deputy Director General of the Department of International Organisations and Conferences at China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, headed the Chinese delegation. The talks addressed civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights, cooperation in multilateral human rights forums, the implications of artificial intelligence for human rights and collaboration on penal systems. Continued concerns over restrictions on Tibetan language education, cultural expression and religious freedom were also highlighted. The Tibetan Bureau warned that China’s ethnic unity legislation could further threaten the distinct identities and traditions of minority communities if their fundamental rights are not adequately protected, as highlighted by CTA. The Tibet Bureau also urged Switzerland to maintain its engagement with Beijing and continue raising issues affecting Tibetans in future diplomatic discussions. Sustained international attention and meaningful action are essential to protecting fundamental freedoms and preserving Tibet’s linguistic, cultural and religious heritage, as reported by CTA. (ANI)
